newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bankers say opposed to minimum reserves.
newsitem.headline: French bankers say opposed to minimum reserves.

text.p: The French bankers association (AFB) repeated on Friday its opposition to the imposition of minimum reserves by the future European Central Bank (ECB) and said if these were imposed they should pay interest.

Earlier the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner of the ECB, said it was preparing the basis to allow the use of minimum reserves as a policy tool but would leave the final decision on whether these would be used and what form they would take to the ECB itself.
"We are against the principle of imposing minimum reserves because this would represent a cost which would be passed on into interest rates," a spokeswoman for the AFB said.
"If they are imposed, we would like them to be remunerated," she said.
French monetary authorities are believed to be keen on the idea of using minimum reserves to control money market volatility.

Otherwise they argue the future European Central Bank would be obliged to conduct daily "fine tuning" operations of the type currently carried out by the Bank of England to smooth volatility in money market rates.
But commercial banks have lobbied hard against the imposition of minimum reserves, which they say would put banks inside monetary union at a disadvantage.
